template.name: Deposition Contradiction Finder
template.description: Flag candidate contradictions between a witness's deposition testimony and the rest of the matter record (other documents, emails, prior statements). Grounded in matter-scoped retrieval; every finding carries a citation you verify. Produces a structured Word deliverable.
template.verificationNote: Verify every flagged contradiction against the original transcript before use. AI can misread nuance, context, or page breaks.

steps.name: Deposition Details
steps.description: Provide the transcript excerpts and the key claims you want scrutinized

questions.question: Matter name
questions.description: The case or matter name as you track it in your files.

questions.question: Witness name
questions.description: Full name of the deponent whose transcript you are analyzing.

questions.question: Deposition date
questions.description: Date the deposition was taken. Used for citation purposes in the output.

questions.question: Key claims to scrutinize
questions.description: The specific factual assertions or storyline elements you want to test for consistency. Be specific — the more targeted this list, the more useful the output.
questions.placeholder: e.g., Witness claims she never received the email. Witness claims the meeting on March 3 never happened. Witness claims she had no supervisory role over the plaintiff.

questions.question: Deposition transcript excerpts
questions.description: Paste the relevant portions of the deposition transcript. Include page and line numbers (e.g., "P. 42:3-18") for each excerpt — the analysis will reference them. You can paste multiple excerpts; separate them with a blank line.
questions.placeholder:
P. 42:3-18
Q: Did you receive the email?
A: No, I never received anything from him.

P. 87:9-21
Q: How often did you communicate with the plaintiff?
A: Rarely. Maybe once or twice a quarter.

questions.question: Prior statements to compare against (optional)
questions.description: Paste excerpts from earlier sworn statements, affidavits, interrogatory answers, or prior deposition testimony. If none, leave blank. Including these allows the analysis to flag contradictions between this deposition and earlier statements.
questions.placeholder: e.g., Affidavit dated January 10, 2026: "I received the email from Mr. Johnson and forwarded it to my supervisor immediately."

steps.name: Flag Contradictions (cited)
steps.description: Retrieve the matter record, flag candidate contradictions, verify each citation, and produce a Word deliverable

config.retrievalQueryTemplate: Testimony and statements by {{witnessName}} relevant to: {{keyClaimsToScrutinize}}. Deposition excerpts: {{depositionExcerpts}}. Prior statements: {{priorStatements}}
config.verificationBanner: Each finding below was flagged by an AI associate and carries a citation. Verify every quote and page/line reference against the original transcript and source before relying on it.
config.systemPrompt: You are a methodical, citation-focused legal research assistant helping a licensed attorney organize and analyze deposition testimony. You never provide legal advice and always frame your output as a starting point for the attorney's review. You do not speculate beyond what the record supports, and you never fabricate a citation. If the record is ambiguous, you note the ambiguity rather than resolve it.

interview_answers.keyClaimsToScrutinize: Whether Johnson forwarded documents to his personal email or all materials stayed on company servers. The deadline he was given for his written response to the compliance review. How many weeks of severance he was offered.
interview_answers.depositionExcerpts: Q. Did you preserve those documents? A. I believe I did. I forwarded them to my personal email for safekeeping. Q. Did Mr. Weston tell you a deadline for submitting the explanation? A. He said I had until October 17, 2025 to submit my written response. Q. At the time of your termination, did anyone at Nexus Dynamics explain the severance package being offered? A. Sandra Liu gave me a document describing a four-week severance.

statementA.quote: I had already saved all the relevant documentation.

statementB.quote: You didn't save any documents at all.

analyze-contradictions_findings.conflictRationale: The witness claims they saved all necessary documents in statementA, but in statementB, it is suggested that no documents were saved.
followUpQuestions: Can you explain why you said both? Did you change your method or was there a misunderstanding about what documents to save?

statementA.quote: He said I had until October 17, 2025 to submit my written response.

statementB.quote: Johnson was given a deadline of **October 10, 2025** to submit his written explanation.

analyze-contradictions_findings.conflictRationale: The witness and the incident summary report conflicting deadlines for submitting the written response.
followUpQuestions: Can you explain why there is this discrepancy? Was the correct date not communicated or was it a misunderstanding?

statementA.quote: I was offered four weeks of severance.

statementB.quote: **eight (8) weeks of base salary continuation** in accordance with company policy for employees with five or more years of service.

analyze-contradictions_findings.conflictRationale: The witness and the incident summary report conflicting information about the severance package offered.
followUpQuestions: Can you explain why there is this discrepancy? Was there a mistake in the communication or a misunderstanding?
